name: Should I build a ground-floor in-law suite addition or convert existing basement space?

mainEntity.name: Should I build a ground-floor in-law suite addition or convert existing basement space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building a ground-floor addition provides zero-step entries and easier long-term accessibility, but it consumes yard space and requires foundation excavation. Converting an existing basement or building a second-story addition preserves your outdoor footprint and can lower structural costs, but stairs can present mobility barriers for aging relatives unless you add specialized lifts. Ground-level additions also make it simpler to incorporate independent exterior entrances and dedicated patios. Evaluating your property's lot lines, yard use, and the long-term physical mobility needs of your family members helps determine whether building outward or remodeling an existing level is the better path.
acceptedAnswer.description: A ground-floor addition ensures step-free accessibility but uses yard space, while a basement conversion preserves outdoor space but introduces stair-related mobility tradeoffs.
